title: idkOS v1.3.0 启动失败归因：ADV 固件被按 Cardputer 机型审查

execution.environment: macOS arm64; native QEMU ESP32-S3; m5stack-esp-emulator @ 55e5763e; Device Service v1

checks.name: failure stage classification
checks.detail: ROM and app run; failure in guest I2C init; no QEMU assertion, no illegal instruction, flash and partition contract valid

checks.name: review session on cardputer (K132)
checks.detail: 3x i2c_set_pin scl==sda, 2x Interrupt wdt timeout on CPU1, 174 B black frame

checks.name: controlled rerun on cardputer (K132)
checks.detail: same i2c_set_pin error; 649 B frame shows firmware DEVICE CHECK / ADV not detected; serial stops after NVS errors

checks.name: controlled rerun on cardputer-adv (K132-Adv), first session
checks.detail: ready in 8.7 s; 9972 B frame, 7357 non-black pixels, 314 colors; no i2c error, no panic

checks.name: controlled rerun on cardputer-adv (K132-Adv), second session
checks.detail: same 9972 B frame; frame SHA-256 identical to first session

checks.name: issue deduplication
checks.detail: no matching open/closed issue for idkOS, scl==sda, or ADV-to-non-ADV routing; #230 and #234 checked and differ

checks.name: simulator issue filing
checks.detail: intentionally not filed: failure not attributable to the emulator

checks.name: ELF symbolization
checks.detail: no matching ELF available for the review job or reruns

checks.name: full idkOS application function
checks.detail: only first frame verified; Wi-Fi, SSH, calendar, themes not exercised

checks.name: 60 s observation protocol
checks.detail: ADV sessions confirmed first frame and absence of panic until stop, without the full sampling protocol

notes: Conclusion: not an emulator defect. The ADV-only BIN was routed to the base Cardputer profile because M5Burner metadata declares CARDPUTER.
No simulator, review-service, or metadata code was modified; nothing was pushed to the emulator repository; no issue was opened or closed.
The non-ADV fallback in the firmware initializes I2C with identical SCL/SDA GPIO numbers and then stalls or panics; this is firmware-side behavior on an unsupported model.
